text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley told the Nine Network's Business Sunday program,e yesterday that the Howard government needs to speed up its economic reform agenda and accused it of being overly concerned with non-economic issues, unwilling to take political risks and too ready to blame the Senate for lack of policy progress. Page 1.

A total payment of A$1.5 million has been settled upon by the Victorian Government as compensation to nine former judges of the State's Accident Compensation Tribunal who launched unfair dismissal cases after the government abolished the tribunal in late December 1992. Page 3.

The government is seeking a concrete commitment from Telstra on the expected job losses in each state if privatisation proceeds in an attempt to secure the votes of independent senators Brian Harradine and Mal Colston for its Telstra sale legislation. Page 4.

The Australian Industrial Relations Commission has been told by the Business Council of Australia in a submission to the national wage case that there are strong arguments for a single minimum adult wage of around A$9.19 per hour. The council argues that any minimum wage increases for the low paid be traded off against increased unemployment. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following News Limited executive chairman Ken Cowley's attack on the federal government for using a hostile Senate as an excuse for failing to implement crucial economic reforms, the federal government will this week implement a strategy to form a series of triggers that may lead to a double dissolution election in 1998. Page 1.

News Limited chief executive Ken Cowley has indicated the News Corporation is interested in increasing its holding in the Seven Network, but is no longer interested in taking control of John Fairfax. Cowley said that although he feels the federal government is more sympathetic to the Packer family's view on media ownership than to News's, he does hope Canadian Conrad Black will retain control of Fairfax. Page 1.

Department of Health and Family Services documents indicate the best option for pensioners who are forced to pay large up front fees to enter nursing care is to sell their family home. The documents will make it difficult for the federal government to honour commitments made by Family Services Minister Judi Moylan, who promised to protect people who pay the fees in the August budget. Page 1.

A landmark native title claim by the Larrakia Aboriginal people, which covers all undeveloped Crown land in Darwin and the surrounding area, including beaches, reserves and parks, has been backed by the powerful Northern Land Council. The move has caused the Northern Territory Government to demand that federal legislation ban claims over capital cities. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A plan that has the backing of Federal Arts and Communications Minister Richard Alston will move to scrap restrictions on the amount of the media that large proprietors can control and instead regulate ownership by the general competition laws. Page 1.

University of New South Wales vice-chancellor Professor John Niland will today put his reputation on the line over plans to overhaul the university's administration. The UNSW governing council will debate a A$20 million cost-cutting package that could see two faculties, 26 courses, and 100 jobs axed. Page 1.

A fire that killed four people at Seven Hills yesterday morning may have been started by a young child playing with matches. Police believe the four victims, David Goding, 24, his de facto wife Tracey Caulton, 21, and two of their children, may have survived had a smoke detector been installed in the home. Page 1.

Immigration Minister Philip Ruddock has defended Federal Government plans to decrease the number of immigrants to Australia by clamping down on sham marriages and de facto relationships. Under the plan, some overseas embassies will be allocated with extra staff to interview overseas applicants for spouse visas more thoroughly. Page 3.
THE AGE

A series of early morning raids on homes and licensed brothels in Melbourne by immigration and taxation officers over the weekend has broken an elaborate international prostitution ring. The operators of the racket were bringing Thai women into Australia and forcing them into prostitution. Page A1.

Returning from a meeting with Asian education ministers in Thailand, Victoria Tertiary Education Minister Phil Honeywood has warned the race debate sparked by Pauline Hanson may see Victoria lose up to a third of the lucrative international student market due to student fears of a racial backlash. Page A1.

A Victorian study of judges, magistrates and lawyers, conducted by the Federation of Community Legal Centres, has revealed that an increase in guilty pleas by defendants with valid defences is a result of cuts to legal aid. Federal funding cuts had also put at risk those unable to afford Family Court intervention orders against domestic violence. Page A1.

Senior research fellow at the Australian Institute of Family Studies, Helen Glezer, has conducted a study into the working patterns of men and women and found that men still want to be full-time workers while less than 30 hours each week would suit most women. Page A3.
